evidence.intree_statement: Class Isomorphism (x y : C) : Type := { to : x ~> y; from : y ~> x; iso_to_from : to ∘ from ≈ id; iso_from_to : from ∘ to ≈ id }.
Class IsIsomorphism {x y : C} (f : x ~> y) := { two_sided_inverse : y ~> x; is_right_inverse : f ∘ two_sided_inverse ≈ id; is_left_inverse : two_sided_inverse ∘ f ≈ id }.
Lemma comp_inverse_unique {C : Category} {x y : C} (f : x ~> y) (g g' : y ~> x) : f ∘ g ≈ id[y] -> g' ∘ f ≈ id[x] -> g ≈ g'.
Program Definition iso_compose {x y z : C} `(f : y ≅ z) `(g : x ≅ y) : x ≅ z := {| to := to f ∘ to g; from := from g ∘ from f |}.

statement_record.book: e : a -> b is invertible when there is e' : b -> a with e' e = 1_a and e e' = 1_b; e' is unique when it exists (written e^{-1}); and (e1 e2)^{-1} = e2^{-1} e1^{-1} when the composite is defined and both factors invertible.
statement_record.intree: Class Isomorphism packages to/from with iso_to_from and iso_from_to (both laws under ≈); IsIsomorphism is the single-morphism predicate form; comp_inverse_unique proves a right inverse and a left inverse of the same f agree (whence uniqueness of two-sided inverses, also to_equiv_implies_iso_equiv at line 317); iso_compose realizes the composite iso with inverse from g ∘ from f, the reversed-order law as definitional content.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same — setoid rephrasing with ≈; the reversed-inverse law is carried as the definition of iso_compose (its from-component) plus uniqueness of inverses rather than as a standalone equation, which is the same content up to presentation.

All quotes re-read and accurate; file registered in _CoqProject:444. strength_comparison honest: the anti-homomorphism law is definitional content of iso_compose plus inverse uniqueness, same substance.

evidence.intree_statement: Class Section `(f : x ~> y) := { section : y ~> x; section_comp : section ∘ f ≈ id }.
Class Retraction `(f : x ~> y) := { retract : y ~> x; retract_comp : f ∘ retract ≈ id }.
Definition SplitEpi `(f : x ~> y) := Retraction f.  Definition SplitMono `(f : x ~> y) := Section f.
Lemma retractions_are_epic : Retraction f → Epic f.
Lemma sections_are_monic : Section f → Monic f.
Definition flip_Section {C : Category} `(f : x ~> y) (s : @Section C x y f) : @Retraction C y x section.  (and dually flip_Retraction at line 241)

statement_record.book: A right inverse (section) of h : a -> b is r : b -> a with h r = 1_b; a left inverse is a retraction. An arrow with a right inverse is epi (converse holds in Set, fails in Grp); one with a left inverse is monic. When g h = 1_a, g is a split epi, h a split monic, and the composite f = h g is an idempotent.
statement_record.intree: Section/Retraction classes carry exactly the one-sided inverse data under ≈; SplitEpi/SplitMono name them; retractions_are_epic and sections_are_monic prove both implication claims; flip_Section/flip_Retraction record the duality between the two roles of a split pair.

evidence.intree_statement: Class Idempotent `(f : x ~> x) := { idem : f ∘ f ≈ f }.

evidence.intree_statement: Class ZeroObject (C : Category) := { zero_terminal : @Terminal C; zero_initial : @Initial C; zero_coincide : @initial_obj C zero_initial ≅ @terminal_obj C zero_terminal }.

statement_record.book: A null (zero) object z is both initial and terminal; it is unique up to isomorphism; for any a, b the unique composite a -> z -> b is the zero arrow, and any composite with a zero arrow is a zero arrow. Examples: Ab, R-Mod, Set*.
